page: Amazon Web Services m5.12xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the AWS Nitro System. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor operating at 3.1 GHz, it features 48 dedicated vCPUs spanning 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The memory subsystem provides 192.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Cache resources include 32 KB L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a shared 35 MB L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX and AVX-512 extensions.

Storage and networking architecture relies on external services, as the instance includes no local bundled storage. Network performance is provisioned with a 12 Gbps baseline bandwidth. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs bundled in this instance type. Resource management and virtualization are offloaded to dedicated Nitro hypervisor hardware, minimizing host-level compute contention.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier multi-threaded output, registering 40,455.21 in stress-ng multi-core tests, 10,676.0 in Geekbench multi-core, and 34,538.76 in PassMark CPU score. However, single-core execution reflects lower efficiency, categorized in the lower tier for stress-ng single-core performance (1,383.8) and gzip compression (23.64 GB/sec). Memory throughput reaches 108.48 GB/sec for uncached large reads and 47.89 GB/sec for writes. The instance delivers 37.99 million Redis SET operations per second and 27.06 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The instance delivers balanced resource allocation without premium hardware premiums like local NVMe or GPU accelerators. Given its solid multi-core throughput and 192 GB memory footprint, the m5.12xlarge is suitable for enterprise web backends, container orchestration, mid-scale relational databases, batch processing, and CI/CD compilation pipelines.
